findings.title: Blocking flock with no timeout — hung sync process blocks all other commands indefinitely
findings.description: unix.Flock(fd, LOCK_EX) blocks the calling goroutine (and thus the entire ccp process) with no timeout. If a `ccp sync pull` hangs waiting on a slow network response while holding the lock, every other ccp command — profile create, profile use, profile delete — blocks forever at the flock call. There is no LOCK_NB path, no deadline, no stale-lock detection, and no way for the user to break the deadlock short of killing the hung process. POSIX flock is not broken on process death (the lock releases automatically when the fd is closed), so a crashed process does not leave a stale lock — but a hung live process does.
findings.recommendation: Add a non-blocking attempt first: try LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB, and if it fails with EWOULDBLOCK, either fail immediately with a helpful message ('another ccp is running; use ccp unlock to force-release or wait') or spin with a configurable deadline (e.g. 30 s) using a ticker and LOCK_NB retries.

findings.title: manifest.Load called before the lock is acquired — TOCTOU on manifest reads
findings.description: loadState() reads manifest.toml at line 27 and returns the Manifest value to the caller. All mutating commands (profile_create, profile_delete, profile_rename, profile_use, sync_push, sync_pull) then call withLock() with the already-loaded state. The lock is only acquired AFTER the manifest has been read. A concurrent process that races through loadState + withLock + saveManifest between the first process's loadState and its withLock will have its manifest write silently overwritten when the first process later calls saveManifest(s) with its stale copy of s.Manifest. The manifest mutation (ActiveProfile change, etc.) is lost.
findings.recommendation: Move manifest.Load inside the withLock closure, or re-read and validate the manifest inside the lock before writing. The pattern should be: acquire lock → read → mutate → write → release.

findings.title: No timeout on go-git network operations — Push, Pull, and CloneOrOpen hang forever on unreachable remote
findings.description: Push() at line 246 calls repo.Push() with no context. Pull() at line 307 calls w.Pull() with no context. CloneOrOpen() at line 418 calls git.PlainClone() with no context. go-git honors context.Context cancellation when passed via PushOptions.Context, PullOptions.Context, and CloneOptions.Context, but none of these call sites pass one. If the remote (GitHub, self-hosted git server) is unreachable or the SSH handshake stalls, the process hangs indefinitely while holding the global flock, which in turn blocks all other ccp processes (see REL-001).
findings.recommendation: Create a context.WithTimeout (e.g. 60 s for push/pull, 120 s for clone) in the command layer, pass it down through PushOptions.Context, PullOptions.Context, and CloneOptions.Context. Propagate the timeout error with a user-friendly message.

findings.title: Delete: second Rename failure leaves partial state with source dir gone and runtime dir orphaned
findings.description: Delete() does two sequential os.Rename calls. The first (line 126) moves pr.SourceDir to srcBackup. If the second os.Rename (line 133, moving pr.ConfigDir to runtimeBackup) fails — e.g. cross-device rename, permission error, disk full — the function returns an error. At this point SourceDir no longer exists at its original location (it was moved to srcBackup), but ConfigDir still exists at its original location and has no SourceDir to pair with. The symlinks in ConfigDir now point into srcBackup (which the user may not know about). There is no rollback of the first Rename.
findings.recommendation: If the second Rename fails, attempt to rename srcBackup back to pr.SourceDir before returning the error, with a clear error message indicating partial state if that recovery also fails.

findings.title: Rename: second Rename failure leaves source dir moved to new name with no runtime dir, old runtime dir orphaned
findings.description: Rename() moves src.SourceDir to dst.SourceDir (line 157). If the subsequent os.Rename of src.ConfigDir to dst.ConfigDir fails (line 161), the function returns that error. At this point the source dir lives at the new name's path, but the runtime (config) dir still exists under the OLD name. The profile is in a split-name state: source says 'new', runtime says 'old'. Symlinks are not yet rebuilt. The profile is effectively broken.
findings.recommendation: If the ConfigDir rename fails, attempt to rename dst.SourceDir back to src.SourceDir before returning the composite error.

findings.title: Create: BuildSymlinks failure after success=false defer — ConfigDir may persist as orphaned directory
findings.description: The defer at line 53 removes pr.SourceDir if success is false. BuildSymlinks() at line 74 calls os.MkdirAll(pr.ConfigDir) before creating any symlinks. If BuildSymlinks returns an error, success stays false, the defer fires and removes SourceDir — but ConfigDir (the runtime directory, ~/.claude-<name>) was already created by os.MkdirAll and is NOT cleaned up. This orphaned empty ConfigDir will cause Exists() to return false (it checks SourceDir only), so a retry of Create will succeed at the SourceDir level but then hit the ensureSymlink path in BuildSymlinks where ConfigDir already exists, which is fine — but the ghost ConfigDir may confuse `profile list` or `profile doctor`.
findings.recommendation: In the defer cleanup block, also remove pr.ConfigDir if it was created by this invocation but SourceDir is being rolled back. Or: only create ConfigDir after all other steps succeed.

findings.title: Rollback: partial move on error leaves successfully-moved profiles restored but remaining ones still in backup
findings.description: The comment at line 85 says 'partial restore is OK because each moved profile is independently valid.' This is true for separate profiles, but within a single profile the moves are ordered: profiles- entry first, then claude- entry. If the claude- rename fails after the profiles- rename succeeded, the profile source dir is restored but the runtime dir is still in the backup. The profile's symlinks now point into a SourceDir that exists but has no corresponding ConfigDir entry in the backup anymore (it's been moved out). The comment's stated invariant does not hold for the within-profile source/runtime pair ordering.
findings.recommendation: Process source and runtime dirs as atomic pairs: attempt both renames for each profile name before moving to the next, or document and test the exact state left on failure.

findings.title: Delete + Prune inside same lock: the just-created backup can be pruned before rollback is possible
findings.description: profile_delete.go calls backup.New, profile.Delete, and then backup.Prune(DefaultRetention=10) all inside the same withLock closure. If the user already has 10 backups, Prune deletes the oldest one — which could be the one created by this very Delete if the timestamp sort puts it earliest. In practice the newly-created backup will have the most recent timestamp and survive, so the immediate-prune risk is low. However, the design means a rollback window of exactly DefaultRetention operations. This is acceptable, but the interaction is undocumented and a user who runs 10 destructive operations rapidly will silently lose the oldest backup.
findings.recommendation: Document the retention-window contract clearly. Consider that Prune removes up to keep=10 total, so after delete+prune there will be at most 10 backups total — the new one included. The risk here is the undocumented interaction, not a correctness bug per se. Low-priority but worth a comment.

findings.title: install.js: no integrity check on downloaded binary — truncated or substituted archive accepted silently
findings.description: The download-and-extract flow in install.js buffers all response bytes (line 65), gunzips, and extracts the ccp binary with no SHA-256 or checksum verification. If the GitHub CDN returns a partial response (network truncation), zlib.gunzipSync will throw — which is caught and results in process.exit(1), so a truncated gzip is caught. However, a correctly-formed tar.gz containing a different or malicious binary (e.g. from a compromised CDN, MITM on a network without HSTS, or a mis-tagged release) will be installed without any integrity signal. There is no comparison against a pinned checksum file.
findings.recommendation: Publish a checksums.txt alongside each release (goreleaser supports this natively). In install.js, download checksums.txt first, verify the SHA-256 of the concatenated chunks before passing to extractBinary. This is a standard supply-chain hardening step for binary distribution via npm.

findings.title: install.js: no request timeout — download hangs indefinitely on stalled connection
findings.description: The https.get call at line 48 has no socket timeout and no request timeout. If the GitHub CDN accepts the TCP connection but then stalls sending data (partial response, slow server), the postinstall script hangs indefinitely, blocking npm install. Node's https.get does not impose a default timeout.
findings.recommendation: Set req.setTimeout(30000, () => { req.destroy(new Error('download timed out')); }) on the ClientRequest returned by https.get.

findings.title: ErrRemoteEmpty matched on error string 'empty' — fragile against go-git version changes
findings.description: CloneOrOpen detects an empty remote with: strings.Contains(err.Error(), "empty") || err == transport.ErrEmptyRemoteRepository. The string match is a fallback for cases where go-git wraps the sentinel error. If a future go-git version changes the error message text (e.g. 'repository is empty' or 'remote has no refs'), the string check silently stops matching, CloneOrOpen returns a generic clone error, and `ccp sync setup --url <new-empty-repo>` fails where it previously succeeded. The sentinel equality check (err == transport.ErrEmptyRemoteRepository) is stable, but wrapping via fmt.Errorf defeats ==.
findings.recommendation: Use errors.Is(err, transport.ErrEmptyRemoteRepository) to handle wrapping correctly, and drop the fragile string match. If go-git wraps it, errors.Is will still unwrap correctly.

findings.title: Manifest schema version 0 silently upgraded — no explicit migration, future required fields silently zero-valued
findings.description: Load() treats SchemaVersion==0 as 'treat as current' by overwriting it (line 51: m.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion). No migration function is called. If a future CurrentSchemaVersion=2 adds a required field, a v0 manifest will load with that field at its Go zero value (empty string, 0, false) and be silently upgraded and written back. The caller has no way to know a migration occurred or that a field was defaulted. There is no 'migrated' flag in the returned state value.
findings.recommendation: For each schema bump, add an explicit migration step that sets new required fields to their correct defaults (not Go zero values) before the manifest is used. Return a boolean or enum indicating whether migration happened so the caller can optionally warn the user.

residual_risks.description: Signal handling: Ctrl-C during a multi-step operation (e.g. profile switch that re-points symlinks) will leave state partially applied. The flock will be released on process exit (fd closes), but the in-progress filesystem mutations will not be rolled back. For single-user local use this is low-risk — the user can re-run the command — but there is no documented recovery path. Confidence too low to file as a primary finding since it requires specific timing and signal delivery.

copyFile in profile.go (line 103) opens the destination with O_TRUNC before the copy completes. A crash mid-copy leaves a truncated file at the destination with no cleanup. The enclosing copyTree is only called during Create (seeding) and Rollback-adjacent operations, so recovery is a re-run of Create. This is acceptable for a CLI tool but worth noting as a non-atomic file copy.

testing_gaps.description: No test covers concurrent ccp processes racing through loadState + withLock + saveManifest. The TOCTOU window in REL-002 is exercisable only with two goroutines or processes running simultaneously.
No test simulates a mid-Delete failure (e.g. second Rename returns an error) to verify that SourceDir is rolled back. REL-004 and REL-005 partial-state paths are untested.
No test exercises CloneOrOpen with a mock remote that returns a wrapped ErrEmptyRemoteRepository to verify the errors.Is path vs the string-match path (REL-011).
